messages:
olivia: Quick note: saved view oddness — I saved a view from a route that pins a model, but when I browse the model page the saved view is missing. Worked on route page. Anyone seen this? :confused:
sam: I hit this too earlier. I think our listing logic only checks route_id when deciding visibility. If scope included model we should surface on model pages as well.
raj: yep backend currently indexes only primary_scope in the new savedview rows. We intended to have cross-ref indexes but that work was never finished.
taylor: For UX, do we want discovery semantics where a saved view that mentions a model shows up on model pages automatically, or require an explicit model-scope at creation? Both have tradeoffs.
mina: My vote: auto-surface if the user's save included the model pin at the time of save. But we have to make it transparent who owns/gets billed. Right now telemetry assumes route charges.
raj: From infra POV, add a small visibility index per savedview containing route_refs and model_refs. Querying that index is cheap. But we should avoid creating duplicate quota entries when surfacing in other contexts.
olivia: Good call. We also need a visible indicator in the UI (e.g., "origin: route / created by X") when a view shows up in a different context so people don't get confused.
sam: Also: ACLs. If model sits in partner org, surfacing could leak access. Need server-side enforcement: only surface if viewer has read access to both route and model or if charge_target is org-level.
taylor: Proposal: savedview schema adds: scopes: ["route","model","org"], origin_context, charge_target, model_refs, route_refs. Listing returns savedviews where current_context ∈ scopes OR current_context ∈ origin_contexts? We should be explicit: include if any ref matches and ACL allows.
raj: Implementation note: secondary index on model_refs (GSI) + precomputed visibility_flags to short-circuit ACL checks for the UI. Visibility_flags is just a small bitset per-savedview indicating which common contexts it's eligible for.
mina: Telemetry: capture fields savedview.create (scopes, charge_target, origin), savedview.surface (surface_context, resolved_charge_target, source_index), and savedview.view_click (clicked_from_context). We'll use these to watch for accidental exposures.
olivia: Save modal UX: default scope should include the things the user had pinned/filtered, but show a small summary: "This view will be visible on: Route /chat, Model: rwkv-13b. Charge target: route /chat" with an edit option.
sam: Quotas: enforce on creation against charge_target only. Discovery/surfacing doesn't increment quotas. If someone tries to set charge_target to a tiny route and they'd exceed quota, block with a helpful error.
raj: Rollout plan: feature flag `savedview_cross_context` behind a canary. Start internal -> 5% -> 25 -> 100. During canary, mark index as "eventual" and add a UI hint when a view might not appear yet due to indexing.
taylor: UI microcopy: when a view is surfaced but charge_target != current_context, show "Origin: route /chat · charge: route /chat" and a link to "View origin". Also an icon indicating cross-bound.
mina: Dashboard work: add a savedview exposure dashboard with metrics: surfacing_rate, missing_surface_errors, cross_context_click_through, and quota_block_rate.
olivia: Action items: 1) Sam: write API contract with new fields. 2) Raj: prototype model_refs GSI and visibility_flags. 3) Mina: telemetry schema + dashboard. 4) Taylor: mockups for save modal + badges + missing-index toast. I'll coordinate canary groups.
sam: started API PR 4712, will ping for review.
raj: will spin up prototype, estimate storage & indexing costs.
mina: will add telemetry events and a gating dashboard, plus alerts for exposure spikes.
deploy-bot: flag `savedview_cross_context` enabled for 5% canary at 2024-12-03T14:12:00Z :rocket:
olivia: thanks team — we'll sync after early canary signals.
